author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
New immigration policy has attracted bipartisan condemnation, with Labor warning it would damage construction, healthcare and agriculture

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation says it will cut the number of temporary migrants in Australia by more than 750,000 over three years, targeting international students and the family members of skilled migrants in a “net-negative” plan.

But Labor has said it would cause sweeping damage to the construction
title: One Nation vows to cut migration by 750,000, sparking fears for key industries including aged care

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Good morning, Krishani Dhanji here with you for another busy sitting week.

There’s a few moving parts in Parliament this week – One Nation has this morning announced a migration plan that will drastically cut temporary visas, and lead to more headache for the Coalition who are asked why Pauline Hanson is driving the agenda and not them.

There’s a role for the Australian government to send a clear signal that electrification is happening and that it’s what the future of our energy system will depend on.

At the moment, federal policy is sending mixed messages.
title: Politics live: electrifying push for Australians to save $5,000 a year; bumper weekend for auctions

author: Keely Aouga
description:
The 8ft statue, installed in Phoenix last week to mark one year since Kirk’s killing, was found painted red

A newly unveiled statue of the rightwing activist Charlie Kirk was vandalized at the Turning Point USA headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona.

The statue was found with red spray-paint. A nearby poster memorial in front of the statue was vandalized with red paint as well.

Continue reading...
title: New Charlie Kirk statue vandalized at Turning Point USA headquarters

author: Roque Planas
description:
Police officer shared location of a woman with his relative who is accused of abusing woman

A San Jose police officer was fired for using his department’s Flock license plate tracking system to share the location of a woman with the suspect accused of abusing her, Chief Paul Joseph told NBC Bay Area on Friday.

The firing marks another in a growing number of cases of misuse of a controversial surveillance technology that has expanded rapidly over the last several years.

Continue reading...
title: San Jose officer fired for misusing Flock camera database in domestic abuse case

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Disturbing and AI-generated versions of Dr Seuss character have been used to threaten schools and communities

Schools and law enforcement authorities in the US are issuing warnings against a viral “Cat in the Hat” social media trend in which disturbing or AI-generated versions of the Dr Seuss character are used to threaten students, schools and communities.

The latest warnings come as safety concerns increase and several teenagers have been arrested or charged over posts connected to the trend.

Continue reading...
title: US schools and police warn about viral ‘Cat in the Hat’ trend after teens’ arrests

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Jefferson county coroner says 40-year-old woman died on Saturday, while two infants died with disease in August

A coroner in Pennsylvania announced the death of a 40-year-old woman associated with the state’s ongoing measles outbreak. The death appears to mark the third in the US state’s ongoing outbreak.

Two previous deaths in the state were in infant children. In one case, the infant was born with a genetic defect that made her vulnerable to infection. The second infant child was infected with measles, and died of a ruptured spleen.

Continue reading...
title: Pennsylvania reports apparent third measles-related death amid outbreak

author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
description:
US president says ‘many people agree’ with his view on unification, brushing off Andy Burnham’s opposition to referendum

Donald Trump has reiterated his support for Irish unification and brushed off Andy Burnham’s opposition to a referendum. “Everybody says that. Then things happen,” the US president said on Sunday of the British prime minister’s response.

“It seems to me that one of the naturals of all time is to put them together,” Trump said of the unification of Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.

Continue reading...
title: Donald Trump doubles down on support for united Ireland

author: Associated Press
description:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany and pilot swim to safety after plane made emergency landing in lake

A Republican congressman said he had to swim to safety after a plane he was traveling in made an emergency landing in a lake late Saturday.

Representative Tom Tiffany says he was returning from the La Crosse county Lincoln Day Dinner when the light aircraft lost power as it approached Wausau downtown airport. The pilot made an emergency landing in Lake Wausau. They both ended up in the water and swam to safety.

Continue reading...
title: Wisconsin congressman swims to safety after plane makes emergency landing in lake

author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem and Seham Tantesh in Gaza
description:
Woman’s family says she died of injuries after being shot in the head while sitting inside a tent near Khan Younis

A pregnant Palestinian woman died on Saturday from injuries sustained after being shot in the head by Israeli forces south of Khan Younis, according to her family and medical workers, as strikes across Gaza killed at least 10 people in 48 hours.

The woman, named as Iman Shalouf, 27, who was nearly eight months pregnant, was sitting inside her family’s tent in the al-Mawasi area when Israeli gunfire struck her, according to paramedics and witnesses.

Continue reading...
title: Pregnant woman among more than 10 killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Ex-president urged party at closed-door fundraiser to create sweeping framework, from safety ‘slow-down’ to job losses

Barack Obama urged Democrats to prioritize a “public conversation” about AI management and safety in a closed-door Manhattan fundraiser last week.

The comments by the former US president reportedly urged the party to create a sweeping framework for everything from a safety “slow-down” to domestic job losses and children’s wellbeing.

Continue reading...
title: Obama reportedly urges Democrats to prioritize safety plan for AI

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Sheriff’s office identifies Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, as person of interest after series of stabbings in Houma leaves four dead

Police are searching for a person of interest after a series of stabbings in Houma, Louisiana, left at least four people dead and another person in critical condition in hospital.

The Terrebonne parish sheriff’s office identified Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, as a person of interest, after deputies were initially called to the Ashland Drive area of Houma and located a juvenile with apparent stab wounds.

Continue reading...
title: Four dead in Louisiana stabbing spree as police search for person of interest

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Harborne and Delo’s cash could buy a massive head start in an election, but spending big has possible pitfalls

Nigel Farage once said he could spend his £5m gift from Christopher Harborne on Ferraris if he wanted to, given its unconditional nature.

With the new donations to his party from Harborne and his fellow crypto billionaire Ben Delo of £72m over the past weekend alone, Farage’s party now has nearly enough cash to buy a Reform UK branded Ferrari for a party organiser in each of Britain’s 632 constituencies (though that would certainly be a waste and a bit of a tax headache).

Continue reading...
title: How could Reform UK spend its £72m of new billionaire donations?

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
The currency has now reached its highest level against the US and Australian dollars in six months

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

In the unpredictable world of global currency markets, there has been one safe bet: that the Japanese yen would continue its relentless decline.

In recent weeks, that trade has started to unravel after Tokyo and Washington intervened to support the longsuffering Japanese currency.

Continue reading...
title: As Japan’s yen peaks, is the era of budget-friendly trips coming to an end for Australian travellers?

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
‘Red lines’ legislation would forbid defence equipment technology or services being used, includes parts for F-35 fighter jets

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Crossbench MPs including David Pocock and Sophie Scamps will put pressure on the Albanese government to ban Australian goods from being used by the Israeli military – including for F-35 fighter jets – by introducing a bill designed to force it to adhere to international obligations.

The group’s “red lines” legislation, to be presented on Monday, would outlaw defence equipment, technology o
title: Crossbench MPs launch push to stop Australian military exports being used in human rights breaches

author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
description:
Exclusive: New details underscoring depth of relationship between billionaire and party revealed in first episode of Guardian podcast The Populist

  • Listen to the Guardian’s podcast The Populist here

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce stayed overnight at Gina Rinehart’s $20m Brisbane mansion after fundraising events held for One Nation, Guardian Australia can reveal.

On one occasion, Joyce conducted a live television interview with Channel Seven’s Sunrise program from a room that appears to be a bedroom in Rinehart’s home.
title: Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce stayed at Gina Rinehart’s $20m mansion after One Nation fundraisers

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Former vice-president and her husband were not home when person entered their property, no arrests were made

Law enforcement officials and a spokesperson for former vice-president Kamala Harris said a trespasser was stopped at her Malibu home in California on Friday night.

Neither the former vice-president nor her husband, Doug Emhoff, were home at the time.

Continue reading...
title: Kamala Harris’s California home targeted by trespasser, officials say

author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
description:
Fire survivors and bereaved urge Barnet Group to ‘reconsider’ appointment of Laura Johnson, who pushed for cheaper contractor

Grenfell survivors and bereaved relatives have criticised the “outrageous decision” to hire a director who oversaw cost-cutting at Grenfell Tower in a £150,000-a-year senior council housing role.

Laura Johnson, the director of housing at the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) at the time of the 2017 Grenfell fire, has been appointed the permanent director of development and property at the Barnet Group, which manages the borough’s 13,000 council homes.

Continue reading...
title: Director who oversaw Grenfell cost-cutting given senior council housing role

author: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor
description:
In a new video, Klein and Taylor outline a ominous evolution taking shape on the far right – and how to stay loyal to this planet and each other

  • The end times fascists are plotting their escape from our world. Our mission is clear

An ominous evolution is under way on the far right. It is a dangerous shift that is linked to our era of existential crises, defined by its pandemics, climate emergencies, resource wars and rogue tech. Today’s fascists are part of a dangerous and fractious alliance – from messianic venture capitalists to army-controlling theocrats – united by the belief that the end of the world is upon us and that only a chosen few deserve to be saved. That is the thesis of Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s new book, End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World.

Since it can be hard to believe that political and corporate leaders
title: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor: the future according to end times fascism

author: Timothy Pratt
description:
Key government meeting this month will consider US bid to try James ‘Fergie’ Chambers over alleged support for Hamas

Attorneys for James “Fergie” Chambers, the US citizen and wealthy donor to leftwing and humanitarian projects worldwide who is currently imprisoned in Madrid and sought in extradition, have submitted a brief ahead of a decisive government meeting on the case.

Meanwhile, Chambers’ partner, the actor and activist Stella Schnabel, met last week with multiple members of the Spanish parliament to assert his innocence.

Continue reading...
title: Pressure builds in Spain to deny US extradition request for leftwing donor

author: Steven Greenhouse
description:
President has hyped growth of federal investment accounts to help US children – for his own political gain

Since returning to the White House, Donald Trump has scrapped rules that made childcare more affordable and pushed to cut funding for the nation’s public schools. But with midterm elections fast approaching and his approval ratings very low, the US president has repeatedly trumpeted a two-month-old program designed to help the nation’s children. That program, unhumbly named “Trump accounts”, calls for the federal government t
title: ‘Trump accounts’ promise to mint child millionaires. Experts have their doubts

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas in New Orleans
description:
Richard Huye charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud in apparent scheme linked to 2021 storm aftermath

The first defendant charged in connection with an alleged major property insurance fraud scheme in the aftermath of Hurricane Ida in 2021 in Louisiana appears poised to plead guilty, if federal criminal court records are any indication.

Richard William Huye III, who faces a count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud while working as an attorney for Texas law firm McClenny Moseley and Associates (MMA), is scheduled to tentatively appear at a rearraignment hearing on 28 September, filings in New Orleans’s federal courthouse show.

Continue reading...
title: Lawyer charged over alleged insurance fraud after Hurricane Ida poised to plead guilty

author: Press Association
description:
Ex-Tory chancellor says economy has ‘fallen off a cliff’ since Brexit but rejoining union could be ‘quite simple’

Former chancellor George Osborne said Britain’s economy has “fallen off a cliff” since Brexit and that rejoining the European Union’s customs union would be the fastest route to recovery.

Osborne, who resigned as chancellor after being part of David Cameron’s cabinet at the time of the referendum, said it was important to rebuild links with the EU.

Continue reading...
title: George Osborne calls for UK to rejoin EU customs union and boost trade

author: Rob Davies
description:
Exclusive: Supermarket joins line of firms and sports stars including Bellingham and Haaland to have their image hijacked via ads

Tesco has alerted City of London police after it became the latest in a string of companies and sports stars, including Barclays bank and Lewis Hamilton, to have its image hijacked in a “scam” by unlicensed casinos advertising via Facebook and Instagram.

The supermarket chain is among several household-name businesses to have been targeted in an apparent effort by casinos that cannot legally operate in Britain to capitalise on their brand recognition.

Continue reading...
title: Tesco alerts police as supermarket becomes latest victim of scam ‘endorsement’ ads

author: Cait Kelly and Lisa Cox
description:
South Australian authorities say case discovered on Kangaroo Island is first for species of which less than 12,000 animals remain

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

South Australia has recorded the first death of an endangered Australian sea lion from H5 bird flu.

Experts say about 12,000 Australian sea lions remain – though a more recent estimate put the figure at less than 10,000. Most of the population are found in South Australia, with the remainder in Western Australia.
title: First H5 bird flu death of endangered Australian sea lion recorded amid fears for small population

author: Hilary Osborne
description:
Criticism of three-year threshold repayment freeze prompts update to guidance warning terms and conditions could change

University students taking out student loans are to be warned that the terms and conditions could change so they are better informed about what they are signing up to, the government has said.

In July, a report by MPs said slideshows that compared student loan repayments to the cost of a mobile phone contract, and YouTube videos that did not mention the fact that conditions could be altered amounted to mis-selling by the government.

Continue reading...
title: UK government to offer clearer guidance on student loans after repayment row

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Rhun ap Iorwerth, the first non-Labour Senedd leader, questions Westminster’s willingness to relinquish powers

Andy Burnham has to be serious about devolution and understand that Wales is a nation and “not a region in England”, according to the country’s first minister.

Rhun ap Iorwerth, who is the first non-Labour leader of the Senedd since devolution, told the Guardian that while he was encouraged by initial discussions with the new UK prime minister, he was wary about Burnham being captured by a consensus Westminster view against relinquishing further powers.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham must understand Wales is ‘not a region in England’, says first minister

author: Ben Smee
description:
Screen limits will become mandatory in NSW schools from 2028 as federal education minister says students may need a ‘digital detox’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government has announced it will implement limits on screen time in public school classrooms and push for students to take part in daily “pen and paper” learning.

The state’s new regulations follow a similar annou
title: NSW to put strict caps on screen time in classrooms while pushing for ‘pen and paper’ learning

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Liberal MP says One Nation leader is ‘not the person I thought she was’ and he feels ‘sorry’ for Joyce

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Andrew Hastie has vowed to go “all the way” in his fight with Pauline Hanson, as he su
title: Andrew Hastie vows to go ‘all the way’ in Pauline Hanson fight as Joyce denies ‘buyers’ remorse’ claim
